correctness.rationale: For any existing equal-order hexagon, bipartiteness and the girth force unique outward tree layers through distance five, with all q+1 neighbors of a distance-six vertex at distance five. This gives the intersection array, N, and seven eigenvalues via the tridiagonal determinant. On the zero-sum subspace the simple eigenmode at -(q+1) is the point-minus-line vector. Independent radial eigenfunctions recover all three lists of spectral difference tails in RESULT §§1–2. In the summation by parts each negative H3 or H5 can be bounded using the adjacent power increments: the ratios decrease in p by integral averaging of log x on successive intervals, and their p→0 limits satisfy the stated 3/2 and 5/4 bounds. Positive H3 or H5 needs no lower bound from that ratio. The resulting paired sums are positive for q≥3 using |theta|≤q; at q=2 and theta=+sqrt(2) the first coefficient is 2−sqrt(2)/2>0 so Delta4≥Delta6 gives combined lower bound (5−3sqrt(2))Delta6, and at theta=0 the increments are convex as integrals of the convex derivative p x^(p−1). The remaining q=2 signs satisfy the paired bounds directly. F_q(0)=−1 and F_q(1)>0; at any root in (0,1) the other sectors are strictly negative. Li–Weston then excludes any later admissible exponent or second root in that interval. Centering the squared distances leaves exactly one extra null vector at the endpoint. Taylor inversion at p=O(q^−5), with F''=O(q^5) there, yields the stated two terms and error. The analytic proof is universal and does not assume existence at all integer q.
residual_risks: Bounded arithmetic checks are not an enumeration of geometries or a formal audit of the cited general theorems.
